name: Proxmox_VE_Cluster_CephOSD
description: Per-OSD state, fill level and latency for a Proxmox VE hyper-converged Ceph cluster.
technicalNotes:
BatchScript. /nodes/{node}/ceph/osd returns the whole CRUSH tree rather than that node's OSDs -- every node answers with the same cluster-wide map -- so one call discovers and collects every OSD in the cluster. This module is O(1), not O(nodes). Online nodes are tried in turn only until one answers, so a node being down costs nothing. Requires Sys.Audit or Datastore.Audit on /.

The response is {flags, root}, where root is a recursive bucket tree: datacenter and host buckets carry 'children' lists and OSDs are the leaves. Proxmox's own source carries a 'fixme: return a list instead of extjs tree format?' against this endpoint, so the tree is walked rather than assumed to be any particular depth, and the walk is iterative.

The wildvalue is the OSD name (osd.12), which is cluster-unique, deliberately without the host. An OSD's host is a CRUSH placement that can change, and an id built from it would be destroyed by a rebalance -- the same reasoning that governs guest instance ids. The host travels as an instance property, where it is free to change.

Which fields an OSD carries depends on what Ceph could report. status, in, crush_weight, reweight, device_class and pgs come from `osd df tree`; total_space, bytes_used and percent_used from `osd df`; the latencies from the perf dump. A down OSD commonly reports state but no usage and no latency, so each of those is withheld when absent. A zero fill on a down OSD would read as an empty, healthy disk.

NoOutFlagSet reports the cluster-wide noout flag on every OSD instance. noout suppresses rebalancing when an OSD goes down; it is set deliberately during maintenance and then forgotten, which is how a cluster ends up degraded and quiet. The endpoint shape and every field name came from pve-manager PVE/API2/Ceph/OSD.pm; the CRUSH tree is still walked rather than assumed to be any particular depth, because one cluster's layout is not the schema.

Applies on the cluster role: resources whose pve.cluster.role is active or standby, which the NetScan sets. Only one of the pair collects -- the active resource, or the standby while the active one is down or has lost quorum. The other prints nothing, so its datapoints read No Data and the pair never alerts twice. The suite has no addCategory_* PropertySource: the NetScan sets the categories and pve.cluster.role, and the product page lists them for a resource added by hand.

Units: UsedBytes in bytes, as Ceph reports it; latencies in milliseconds. MB and GB are decimal (10^6 and 10^9 bytes); the product page states the suite's convention.

datapoints.name: Up
datapoints.description: 1 when the OSD is up. A down OSD is not serving data.
datapoints.alertBody:
Ceph OSD ##INSTANCE## is down. Check NoOutFlagSet before acting: if noout is set this may be planned maintenance.

Status: ##ALERTVALUEDISPLAYSTATUSNAME## (##VALUE##).

datapoints.name: OSDIn
datapoints.description: 1 when the OSD is in the cluster. An OSD that is up but out is deliberately excluded from data placement, typically during a planned drain.

datapoints.name: NoOutFlagSet
datapoints.description: 1 when the cluster-wide noout flag is set, which suppresses rebalancing when an OSD goes down. Reported on every OSD because it changes what a down OSD means.

datapoints.name: UsedPercent
datapoints.description: OSD fill level. Ceph blocks writes at its full ratio and degrades well before it, and rebalancing needs free space to work with.
datapoints.alertBody:
Ceph OSD ##INSTANCE## is ##VALUE##% full. When any one OSD reaches Ceph's full ratio the cluster stops accepting writes, so a single unbalanced OSD can halt writes for every guest on Ceph.

This started at ##START##, ##DURATION## ago.

datapoints.name: UsedBytes
datapoints.description: OSD raw capacity in use, bytes.

datapoints.name: CrushWeight
datapoints.description: The OSD's weight in the CRUSH map, normally its size in TiB.

datapoints.name: Reweight
datapoints.description: Override weight, 0.0 to 1.0. Below 1.0 means the OSD has been manually or automatically down-weighted.

datapoints.name: PlacementGroups
datapoints.description: Placement groups currently mapped to this OSD. A large imbalance across OSDs indicates a CRUSH or weighting problem.

datapoints.name: CommitLatencyMs
datapoints.description: Ceph commit latency for this OSD, milliseconds.

datapoints.name: ApplyLatencyMs
datapoints.description: Ceph apply latency for this OSD, milliseconds.
